ios.desc:
Documents by Readdle is your file manager, document viewer, PDF editor, and archive extractor for iPhone and iPad. Browse and organize your files, extract ZIP and RAR archives, edit and sign PDFs, and convert or compress anything — all from one app.

FILE MANAGER
- Browse, organize, and manage local files and folders in one fast file browser, rename and color-tag them for quick access
- Import files from your computer, download files directly from the web browser, or work with iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive, and other cloud drives without downloading them


ZIP & RAR ARCHIVE EXTRACTOR
- Unzip and extract ZIP and RAR archives directly on your iPhone or iPad
- Create new ZIP archives to compress and share multiple files at once
- Compress large files and folders to save storage space

PDF EDITOR, VIEWER & CONVERTER
- View and read PDFs, books, and scanned documents with a fast built-in viewer
- Edit or modify existing text directly inside a PDF
- Highlight, add notes, and place stickers on PDFs and books
- Merge multiple PDFs into one, or split, rotate, and reorder pages
- Convert PDF to Word, JPG, PNG, HEIC, and other formats

SIGN DOCUMENTS
- Add your signature to PDF contracts and forms in seconds
- Fill out forms and place text, checkmarks, and initials anywhere on a document
- Store signed contracts securely and access them from any device

FILE CONVERTER & COMPRESSOR
- Convert between PDF, DOCX, JPG, JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WEBP, and more in a few taps
- Compress PDFs, photos, and files to reduce size for email or upload limits
- Create PDFs from photos, scans, or documents, and convert them back to editable formats

SCANNER
- Scan receipts, books, and documents with a built-in OCR document scanner
- Save scans as searchable PDFs directly in Documents or your cloud drive

ALSO INSIDE
- Transcribe audio and video to text, then edit or export the transcript
- Use Smart Eraser to remove unwanted objects from photos
- Play music and video, and transfer files to your Mac or PC over Wi-Fi

Documents is an App Store Editors' Choice winner.


Read more about our terms and conditions here:

quotes.text:
Maybe some people use their iPads for Facebook/Twitter/YouTube. I don't give a damn. They're the same boys/girls that were watching celebrity news and other useless TV shows 10 years ago, when you and I were watching "scientific/educational" shows on TV and hacking away with computers.

I'm getting sick of this "iPad is for consumption" thing. How are you going to "produce" something if you haven't learned anything yet? For me, iPad is a learning device. In the past year, I've read maybe 15 (technical) books on my iPad. I wanted to read them for the past 3 years, I had downloaded their ebooks and stashed them neatly in a 'To-Read' folder, but never get to do so on a Mac or PC because of their form factor.

In the past 2 weeks alone, I read 'JavaScript: The Good Parts' and first 5 chapters of 'Git Pro' (ePub, in iBooks), 70% of 'Head-First C' (PDF, in the fantastic ReaddleDocs[1] app) and 20 other technical/"intellectual" articles in Instapaper. Without iPad, I wouldn't have read them.

---

[1]: http://itunes.apple.com/us/app/readdledocs-for-ipad-pdf-viewer/id364901807?mt=8 - Believe me, this app is fantastic.  You don't know how great it is until you use it.

I'm a big fan of Documents by Readdle for iOS because of it's annotations.

I read on my iPad, annotations auto sync to google drive, and it generally works great.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/documents-by-readdle/id364901807
